- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >3%, model often underestimates further decline; add 1–3% downward bias for next 7–14 days.  
- Model frequently overpredicts mean reversion in short-term (1–3 day) horizons; for 30-day forecasts, apply 1–2% downward adjustment if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price volatility is high, model tends to smooth out extremes; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 5–10 days to reflect sentiment uncertainty.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day high, reduce by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 3–5 days), model often fails to anticipate; apply 2–4% downward bias for first 5 days of forecast.
